messages:
Maria Lopez: Drafting a compact runbook for the "tokenflow" lightbench — want to land on a reproducible pipeline to compare speculative decoding vs baseline on a quantized 13B. High level: measure E2E p95, median latency, token cost and small-scope quality (BLEU/chrf + per-example delta).

Kevin Tran: SGTM. A few clarifying Qs: what do you mean by 'small-scope quality'? exact match? we should pick 2 metrics (one lexical + one rank) so we don't chase noise. Also reproducible seeds pls.

Maria Lopez: By small-scope quality I mean: (1) chrF on a curated 2k holdout, (2) per-example delta and rank correlation (Kendall tau) between baseline and spec outputs. If baseline>spec for >1.0% of examples by chrF we flag. Seeds: use paired generation with same seed where possible; see note below about predictor nondeterminism.

Sasha Iyer: Important: the predictor model in speculative flow is nondeterministic if we use temperature >0. Need to freeze predictor to temp=0 or use greedy predictor to get stable compare. Otherwise paired seeds don't match.

Devin Park: Agree with Sasha. Proposed config: predictor greedy (temp=0), generator temp=0.8, top_p=0.95. Quant: q4f16 (weights in 4-bit with fused kernels). Batching: keep batch size 1 for latency p95, run separate throughput with batch=8.

ops-bot: bench/lightbench triggered by @Maria Lopez. Job id: lb-202903-77. Started 5812345682.

QA Sam: Quick note on datasets: use holdout_prompts_v3 (2k) + stress_prompts_short (200) for long-tail. We'll compute per-example chrF and also a short SROUGE-ish summary similarity to detect hallucination drift.

Kevin Tran: Nice. How are we handling fallback cases? if speculative predictor is wrong we pay extra tokens and time; need to report distribution of 'wasted' tokens and percent fallbacks. Also track median extra tokens when fallback triggers.

Maria Lopez: Yep. Metrics to log: total tokens generated, tokens_on_path (spec predicted tokens reused), fallback_count, extra_tokens_per_fallback, p95 latency with and without cache warm. We'll also log KV cache hit rate.

Devin Park: Command I used locally for a single run (copy to CI):

```bash
bench run \
  --model llamaX-13b \
  --quant q4f16 \
  --decoding speculative \
  --spec-predictor greedy \
  --spec-steps 2 \
  --generator-temp 0.8 \
  --top-p 0.95 \
  --seed 42 \
  --batch 1 \
  --repeats 200 \
  --dataset holdout_prompts_v3 \
  --log tokenflow_metrics.json
```

ops-bot: bench/lightbench lb-202903-77 finished. baseline: p95=218ms, median=42ms, tokens=1.0x, chrF(avg)=0.642. speculative: p95=148ms, median=31ms, tokens=1.12x, chrF(avg)=0.639. fallback_count=18/200 (9%), extra_tokens_mean=3.2, kv_cache_hit=0.87. Artifacts: s3://bench/lb-202903-77/tokenflow_metrics.json

Sasha Iyer: That looks promising latency-wise. chrF delta -0.003 (~0.5%) — inside tolerance? We had previously said flag >1.0% drop, so no alert. But we should inspect per-example where chrF dropped >5 points.

QA Sam: I'll run the per-example diff and push a CSV for triage. If there are systematic categories (code, math, multi-step) we'll open a follow-up.

Kevin Tran: Also compute Kendall tau on token-level ranking of n-best output lists (paired baseline vs spec) — that helps detect subtle reorder/regression. Even if average chrF okay, ranking mismatch matters.

Maria Lopez: Agreement: action items -> (A) QA Sam: push per-example csv + flagged categories (due EOD), (B) Devin: rerun with predictor=temp0 and predictor=model-shrink (7B) to see if cheaper predictor helps, (C) Ops: run throughput batch=8 sweep and attach trace flamegraphs, (D) Kevin/Sasha: prepare short doc on eval gating thresholds (we keep >1% chrF drop or tau<-0.02 or fallback_rate>12%).

Devin Park: One more experiment suggestion: quantized speculative where predictor uses q2 for predictor-only (if kernel supports). Might reduce predictor cost and slightly alter fallback behaviour — useful to measure tradeoff.

Sasha Iyer: Good idea. Note: when mixing quant levels be careful with fallback compatibility — fallback may need dequant path which adds latency. Log path type for fallback.

Maria Lopez: Thanks all. I'll file a lite PR with the runbook steps and put links to artifacts. If QA flags >20 examples with cat-specific regressions we'll hold the rollout.

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach benchmarks to PR description.

Kevin Tran: Cool, ping me when artifacts are in. I'll run a quick sanity script to compute Kendall and per-example regressions.

Maria Lopez: Will do. Thanks!
